translations.answer: Check if the old constructor sets qMin/qMax as +1e10/-1e10. This order results in qMin > qMax; default explicit setting of position bounds would mask the issue, but setting only velocity bounds may trigger infeasibility. The default values have been merged into PR #159, setting qMin = -1e10 and qMax = +1e10. The old version also needs to be explicitly set to the correct position bounds before use.
translations.applicability: Applies to TSID old versions with incorrect default values; if the caller always explicitly sets position bounds, this specific error will not directly trigger.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and there is no conflict. It has been formally documented or independently reproducible.

translations.details.diagnostics.0: Print or check the qMin/qMax after TaskJointPosVelAccBounds is constructed; confirm if the position bounds are explicitly set before use.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Use merged PR #159, setting qMin = -1e10 and qMax = +1e10; the old version can also explicitly set the correct position bounds to avoid relying on the incorrect default values.

translations.details.outcomes.0: PR #159 was merged on 2022-03-02; the maintainer later confirmed the issue was resolved with PR #159.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why might QP become infeasible when only velocity bounds are configured but the default position bounds are used?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Check the actual bounds after configuration in real-world scenarios; do not rely solely on the default maximums as safety limits.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The constructor sets qMin and qMax in the wrong order, with the negative sign swapped.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Default qMin = +1e10, qMax = -1e10; this leads to qMin > qMax; using the default position bounds may result in infeasible constraints.
